passage: In the hostel common room, Dilnaz told everyone she was going to try out for the lead in the school play. Maria, sitting on the arm of the sofa, gave a small smile with one corner of her mouth higher than the other. Dilnaz stopped mid-sentence. Was that a smirk? Did Maria think she would fail? She kept talking but felt her cheeks warming. Later, in the corridor, Dilnaz asked, "What was that smile about?" Maria blinked. "What smile? Oh. My mouth does that when I am shy about saying I think you would be great." Dilnaz laughed and admitted she had already been reading it as mockery.

qa.q: Where did Maria sit in the common room?
qa.a: Maria sat on the arm of the sofa.

qa.q: What did Dilnaz think Maria's smile meant?
qa.a: She feared it was a smirk, that Maria doubted she could win the lead. Her warm cheeks show she was hurt, though the smile turned out to be Maria's shy habit.

qa.q: How could Dilnaz check the meaning of a smile like that?
qa.a: Ask kindly what the smile was about, as she did, before assuming mockery.

qa.q: How might Maria have felt when Dilnaz asked about the smile?
qa.a: She was probably surprised and a bit sorry, since she meant it as encouragement and never noticed her mouth did that.

grounding: An asymmetric smile may be read as teasing or doubt, but may be habit or shyness, and context decides.

passage:
Dear Vandana,

I have to tell you something I have been carrying since the debate. When you smiled that lopsided smile at me during my speech, I decided you were laughing at me. I lost my place and spoke faster, and I did not talk to you afterwards. I was so cross with you all week. Then Priya told me you do that when you are nervous for someone. Is that true? I want to believe it, because I know you, and you are not mean. I should have asked you straight away instead of guessing. Can we talk on Saturday? I will bring the samosas.

Your friend,
Payal

qa.q: What did Payal offer to bring on Saturday?
qa.a: Payal offered to bring the samosas.

qa.q: Why did Payal spend the week feeling cross with Vandana?
qa.a: Payal read the lopsided smile as mockery during the speech, which was upsetting. Now Payal suspects it may have been Vandana's nervous habit, though Payal is not sure.

qa.q: What would you advise Payal to do the next time a smile is unclear?
qa.a: Ask Vandana straight away, since the smile could be warm or mocking, and their friendship gives a good reason to check.

qa.q: How might Vandana feel on reading the letter?
qa.a: Vandana may feel surprised and sad that a nervous smile hurt a friend, and glad Payal wrote and wants to talk.

grounding: A teenager misreads an asymmetric smile as mocking, then checks, since it may be habit or nerves.

passage:
"Neelam, you asked about Karan. Here's what happened.
When I gave my project talk on water saving, I saw Karan in the second row. One corner of his mouth went up. Just one side. I thought, he's laughing at me. My hands started sweating and I rushed the last slide.
After class I avoided him. But on Friday he came up to me and said my talk made him fix the leaking tap at home.
I asked him, 'Then why the smirk?'
He looked confused. 'What smirk? That's just my face when I'm listening.'
Then he did it again, right there, and I laughed. His mouth only goes up on one side. I, Tanvir, spent three days hating a smile."

qa.q: What did Karan fix at home after the talk?
qa.a: The leaking tap.

qa.q: Why did Tanvir rush the last slide?
qa.a: Tanvir felt embarrassed and anxious, reading Karan's one-sided smile as mockery.

qa.q: What would you advise someone who sees a lopsided smile during a talk?
qa.a: Don't assume it's teasing; it may be a habit or a sign of interest, so check later if it bothers you.

qa.q: How might Karan see Tanvir's reaction?
qa.a: Karan was surprised and confused, since his smile was a habit of listening, not a way of mocking.

grounding: A teenager misreads a classmate's asymmetric smile as mockery, then learns it was just his listening habit.

passage:
In our English class, Mr Kumar said, "I once read two hundred pages in one night." Zainab, next to me, smiled with only one side of her mouth.
I couldn't tell what it meant. Was she doubting him? Was it an inside joke? Or was she just amused?
Mr Kumar noticed. "Zainab, you don't believe me?"
She blushed. "No, Sir, I believe you! I just remembered I did the same with a mystery novel and felt sick the next day."
Mr Kumar laughed. "Fair enough. Maybe we both need more sleep."
Later I asked her about the smirk. She said, "My face does that when I'm thinking of something funny. People think I'm being rude."
- Naveen

qa.q: How many pages did Mr Kumar say he read in one night?
qa.a: Two hundred pages.

qa.q: What might Zainab have been feeling when she smiled with one side of her mouth?
qa.a: She was probably amused, remembering her own reading night, though Naveen couldn't tell if it was doubt or amusement at first.

qa.q: What helped clear up the meaning of Zainab's smile?
qa.a: Mr Kumar asked her directly, and later Naveen asked too, which showed it was private amusement, not doubt.

qa.q: How might Mr Kumar see Zainab's smile before she explained?
qa.a: He may have thought she doubted his story, which is why he asked her directly.

grounding: An observer sees a classmate's asymmetric smile, which could mean doubt or amusement, and context clears it up.

passage:
Monday: At lunch, Abhinav said he'd try out for the school play. Karthik gave a lopsided smile, one side of his mouth going up. Abhinav's cheeks went hot. Was Karthik mocking him?
Wednesday: Abhinav avoided Karthik all day, sitting with other friends at lunch. Karthik looked puzzled but didn't say anything.
Friday: After the tryouts, Karthik found him. "Why've you been ignoring me?"
Abhinav blurted, "You smirked when I said I'd try out."
Karthik stared, then laughed. "That's my impressed face! I didn't think you'd dare. It's cool." He did the lopsided smile again.
Abhinav let out a breath. "Next time just say 'cool.'"
"Deal," Karthik grinned.

qa.q: What did Abhinav say he would try out for?
qa.a: The school play.

qa.q: What was Abhinav feeling when Karthik gave the lopsided smile?
qa.a: Abhinav felt embarrassed and hurt, thinking Karthik was mocking him.

qa.q: What helped Abhinav understand Karthik's smile?
qa.a: Talking directly after tryouts showed the smile meant Karthik was impressed, not mocking.

qa.q: How might Karthik have felt while Abhinav ignored him?
qa.a: Karthik probably felt confused and a bit hurt, not knowing why his friend was avoiding him.

grounding: Over a week, a teenager misreads a friend's asymmetric smile as teasing and learns it showed admiration.

passage: Omkar, you think the new boy is smirking at you? First hear your Bhupen Mama's story. At fifteen, in our school in Guwahati, a boy called Pabitra joined my class. Every time I answered in English, one corner of his mouth went up. Just one. I was sure he was laughing at my accent. For a month I avoided him and even told friends he was proud. Then in the football final we were on the same team, and after I scored, he ran up with that same lopsided smile, hugged me and said, very quietly, "Well done." That was his whole smile, Omkar. Half a smile was all his shy face ever managed. We stayed friends for forty years. So before you decide about this boy, watch him somewhere else. Ask him something.

qa.q: When did Bhupen realise the lopsided smile wasn't mocking?
qa.a: In the football final, when Pabitra ran up with the same smile after Bhupen scored, hugged him and said "Well done."

qa.q: What did young Bhupen feel when Pabitra smiled on one side?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed and resentful, sure that Pabitra was laughing at his accent.

qa.q: What turning point in the story changed Bhupen's reading of the smile?
qa.a: Seeing the same half smile in a warm moment on the football team showed it was habit and shyness, not mockery.

qa.q: How might Pabitra have experienced that first month?
qa.a: Pabitra, shy and new, may have felt lonely and confused about why Bhupen kept avoiding him.

grounding: It illustrates a teenager reading a one-sided smile as mockery when it was habit and shyness, and context changing its meaning.
